# Two facts established before the clarify gate, 24 September 2026

## A Claude Code subagent inherits its parent's session id

A subagent was spawned from this clarify session with one instruction: print
`CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID`, the harness's own digest of it, and the names of any
agent-related environment variables. It returned:

```
CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID=<the parent's own value, not repeated here>
digest: 2377cfb62f89
AI_AGENT=<set>
```

That is the same session id and the same digest, 2377cfb62f89, as the session
that spawned it. The raw id is not written here, and the harness refused this
note twice over until it was taken out: `journal.append` matched the value
against the environment and said so, which is the control `sessions.py`
describes and the reason a record carries twelve hex characters of a digest
rather than an id.
and `AI_AGENT` is set to `claude-code_2-1-273_agent` in the parent as well, so it
does not discriminate either. Before this run no journal and no session log on
this machine held a subagent turn, so nothing recorded answered the question.

The consequence: `sessions.current()` cannot tell a subagent from the session
that spawned it. Wherever this ticket says "the session id it came from", the
value is declared by the session that records it, not derived from the
environment. The gate can refuse the case it can see, a review that names the
implementer's own session as the reviewer's, and it cannot detect a value typed
to pass.

## The frontmatter keys the two assistants read

The Claude Code documentation lists `name`, `description`, `tools`, `model`,
`permissionMode`, `maxTurns`, `skills`, `memory`, `isolation`, `mcpServers`,
`hooks` and `omitClaudeMd` for `.claude/agents/<name>.md`, camelCase as spelled
here, and skips a file with invalid YAML or without `name` and `description`
while silently ignoring a key it does not know. A skill may declare
`context: fork` with `agent: <type>` to run in a subagent context. Sources:
code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents.md and code.claude.com/docs/en/skills.md,
read on 24 September 2026.

Silently ignoring an unknown key matters for the generator: a wrong key in a
generated file produces no error anywhere, so the test that pins the rendered
frontmatter is the only thing that will catch it.
